problem: `PrettyJSON`, recommended for HTTP responses, sends stack traces, absolute paths and internal error text to clients
solution: add client-safe Public/PublicJSON serialization

history.subject: feat(errorkit): add client-safe Public/PublicJSON serialization
history.body:
AGENTS.md, the errorkit README and the error.go comment recommended
PrettyJSON for HTTP responses, but PrettyJSON always includes the stack
trace (package, function and file names), the raw payload and the
wrapped error text (driver messages, hostnames, URLs).

- New PublicError type and AppError.Public()/PublicJSON(): code,
  message, id and trace_id only. The message is the Reason for
  client-error classes (Metadata.HTTPStatus 4xx) and
  Metadata.Description (or the HTTP status text) otherwise, so internal
  reasons never reach clients. Nil-safe like the other methods.
- PrettyJSON is unchanged; its doc comment and the README now say it is
  for logs only. The README documents the client-safe responses.
- The hard-coded "market-ecosystem/" path root was already removed by
  R-131 (05f1bce).

Public() is exported so httpserver (R-002) and grpc (R-004) can reuse
the same message policy inside their own envelopes.

Tests: TestPublicJSONOmitsInternalDetails, TestPublicMessageByStatusClass,
TestPublicFallsBackWhenDescriptionIsEmpty, TestPublicJSONNil.

AGENTS.md wording for R-153 (section 4, replace the last rule):
  - HTTP handler responses should serialize `appErr.PublicJSON()` (or
    embed `appErr.Public()`) and use `appErr.Metadata.HTTPStatus`.
    `PrettyJSON()` includes the stack trace, payload and wrapped error
    text: use it for logs only, never in a response.

Item: R-001
Findings: C1-002

problem: `WithErrorOpt` and `PrettyJSON` send `err.Error()` text to HTTP clients
solution: never send internal error text in HTTP replies

history.subject: fix(httpserver)!: never send internal error text in HTTP replies
history.body:
WithErrorOpt copied err.Error() into Reply.Error, so API clients received
"[CODE] reason" text (panic values, provider messages) or, for other
errors, the whole wrapped chain (SQL, hostnames, constraint names). The
Hertz PrettyJSON helper also sent the marshal error text.

Reply gains a `code` field. WithErrorOpt now sets a client-safe code and
message: for an *errorkit.AppError in the chain, its code plus its Reason
for 4xx errors or its Metadata.Description otherwise; for any other error,
ERR_INTERNAL and "Internal server error". The Hertz HTTPContext.WithError
logs the full error server-side through logger.CtxOrGlobal(ctx) with
trace correlation (warn for 4xx, error otherwise) and fills trace_id from
the active span. PrettyJSON logs the marshal failure and replies with a
generic message. The HandlerFunc godoc example no longer sends
err.Error().

R-001 (C1, PublicJSON in errorkit) is not merged on this branch; the
public-message rule here follows the R-001 proposal so P4.XP can switch to
the errorkit helper once both land.

TestReplyOptionApplicators asserted that errors.New("boom") is sent
verbatim; it now asserts the generic public message (the approved
contract).

Item: R-002
Findings: C2-017

BREAKING CHANGE: Reply.Error no longer contains err.Error(). For an
*errorkit.AppError it holds the Reason (4xx) or Metadata.Description, and
the code moves to the new `code` JSON field; any other error is reported
as code ERR_INTERNAL with message "Internal server error". Clients that
parsed the "[CODE] reason" text must read `code` instead. The Hertz
adapter now logs every error passed to HTTPContext.WithError.

problem: Panic recovery sends the panic value and method name to the remote caller
solution: return a fixed message for recovered panics

history.subject: fix(grpc): return a fixed message for recovered panics
history.body:
The recovery interceptors put the panic value and the method name into
the status message sent to the caller. Recovered panics now reach the
client as codes.Internal with the fixed message "internal error" and an
errdetails.ErrorInfo carrying the errorkit code (ERR_SYSTEM_UNEXPECTED)
and the errorkit error ID. The panic value, method and stack are still
logged, keyed by the same ID.

Tests: unary and server-stream panics over bufconn assert the panic text
and method are absent from status.Convert(err).Message(); a log-capture
test asserts the panic value is logged with the client-visible ID.

Item: R-003
Findings: C3-001

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

problem: `ToStatus` puts the errorkit `Reason` on the wire for every code, including `Internal`
solution: keep internal error reasons off the wire in ToStatus

history.subject: fix(grpc)!: keep internal error reasons off the wire in ToStatus
history.body:
ToStatus used appErr.Error() ("[CODE] reason") as the status message for
every code. SDK reasons often embed the underlying error text (driver
errors, hosts, SQL, file paths), so Internal-class failures leaked them to
any remote caller following the documented error path.

The status message now depends on the class of the error:
- client errors (registered HTTPStatus < 500 and a gRPC code other than
  Internal/Unknown/DataLoss) keep "[CODE] reason";
- server errors (HTTPStatus >= 500, or a gRPC code of Internal, Unknown
  or DataLoss) send only the registered Metadata.Description, or
  "internal error" when it is empty.
The errorkit code and error ID stay in ErrorInfo (Reason, Metadata["id"])
for programmatic handling and log correlation.

The plan names Internal/Unknown/DataLoss; the class rule also covers the
codes that R-019 now maps to Unavailable/DeadlineExceeded from 5xx
metadata (e.g. ERR_DB_POSTGRES_UNAVAILABLE), whose reasons carry the same
kind of driver text as the finding's evidence.

New additive API: ToStatusWithPolicy(err, StatusPolicy) with
StatusPolicy.ExposeInternalReasons, which keeps the pre-2.0 behavior for
trusted internal callers. README "Error mapping" documents the policy.

Tests: over-the-wire message per class over bufconn (client-error codes
keep the reason; Internal, Unknown, unregistered, internal-timeout and
Unavailable codes send the description and never the reason), ErrorInfo
code and ID, the empty-description fallback, and the opt-in policy. The
existing mapping table now asserts the description for 5xx codes.

Item: R-004
Findings: C3-002

BREAKING CHANGE: grpc.ToStatus no longer sends the errorkit reason for
server-side errors (registered HTTPStatus >= 500 or gRPC code
Internal/Unknown/DataLoss); the status message is the registered
Metadata.Description (or "internal error"). Use
ToStatusWithPolicy(err, StatusPolicy{ExposeInternalReasons: true}) to keep
the old message for trusted callers.

problem: DSN password leaked in plaintext through the error payload (logs and `PrettyJSON`); Pool-construction errors carry the cause as `Payload`, not `Wrapped`: no `errors.Is/As`, and connect/ping failures serialize as "marshal_failed"
solution: wrap pool errors instead of exposing the raw driver error

history.subject: fix(postgres): wrap pool errors instead of exposing the raw driver error
history.body:
NewPostgresClient stored the pgx error value as the AppError payload. A
*pgconn.ParseConfigError exports the unredacted connection string, so the

solution: redact URL-bearing audit headers; sanitize URLs and provider messages before payloads, logs and spans; redact nested URL error diagnostics

history.subject: fix(httprequest)!: sanitize URLs and provider messages before payloads, logs and spans
history.body:
URL credentials, query-string secrets and upstream error messages
bypassed redaction: the raw URL (with user:pass@ and ?key=...) went into

solution: widen log redaction to tokens, secrets and URL credentials; mask secret/access/signing keys and full URL passwords

history.subject: fix(logger): mask secret/access/signing keys and full URL passwords
history.body:
- Keys such as secret_key, aws_secret_access_key and signing_key

problem: `urlkit.BuildURL` concatenates `base + path` and re-parses it, so `path` can change the host, query or base query
solution: treat BuildURL path as a path, never as URL syntax

history.subject: fix(urlkit)!: treat BuildURL path as a path, never as URL syntax
history.body:
BuildURL concatenated base + path and re-parsed the result, so a path
such as "@evil.com/x" or ".evil.com/x" changed the host, "users" was
glued to the host, "?"/"#" injected a query or fragment, and a base
query swallowed the path.

BuildURL now parses base once and appends path to its path: a missing
leading slash is added, the base query is kept and merged with params,
and a path with "?", "#", a dot segment (also percent-encoded) or an
invalid escape is rejected with ERR_VALIDATION_INVALID_FORMAT. The
README documents the new rules and error reasons.

Item: R-009
Findings: C6-001

BREAKING CHANGE: BuildURL, BuildURLString and MustBuildURL no longer
concatenate base and path. A path containing "?" or "#", "." or ".."
segments or invalid escapes now returns ERR_VALIDATION_INVALID_FORMAT
(MustBuildURL panics), a path without a leading slash gets one, and a
query on base is preserved instead of being corrupted.

problem: `urlkit.JoinPath` keeps `..` segments and accepts scheme-less or non-HTTP bases
solution: reject dot segments in JoinPath and add JoinHTTPPath

history.subject: fix(urlkit)!: reject dot segments in JoinPath and add JoinHTTPPath
history.body:
JoinPath only trimmed slashes, so a segment such as ".." or "a/../b"
(for example an unvalidated resource ID) escaped the base path once the
server normalized it. Segments with a "." or ".." element are now
rejected with ERR_VALIDATION_INVALID_FORMAT; dots inside an element
("v1.2") stay allowed.

JoinPath still accepts any base url.Parse accepts. The new, additive
JoinHTTPPath also requires an absolute http(s) base with a host, so
"foo", "javascript:alert(1)" or "ftp://..." are rejected. The README
gains API sections for both functions.

solution: add server credentials and explicit insecure options

history.subject: feat(grpc): add server credentials and explicit insecure options
history.body:

express a TLS server, and both sides fell back to plaintext silently.

- ServerConfig.Creds, wired through grpc.Creds.
- WithServerInsecure() / WithClientInsecure(): explicit plaintext opt-in

  insecure option is ERR_SYSTEM_CONFIG_INVALID.
- README: "Transport security" section with a plaintext warning (nil
  credentials are meant only for meshes/sidecars terminating mTLS), TLS
  and mTLS wiring, and the Defaults/migration tables updated.

The nil default is unchanged here (additive part); R-012 makes it an
error.

Tests: TLS round trip over bufconn with an in-memory self-signed
certificate (no key material on disk), a plaintext client rejected by a
TLS server, and the Creds/insecure conflict on both sides.

solution: redact URL-bearing audit headers; implement the redacted inbound audit log

history.subject: feat(hertz)!: implement the redacted inbound audit log

commented out: it logged nothing (no audit trail for auth or admin

problem: The retry loop ignores HTTP method idempotency: non-idempotent POSTs, including billable LLM calls, are re-sent up to 5 times
solution: retry only requests that are safe to resend; prevent replay after redirected dial failures

history.subject: fix(httprequest): prevent replay after redirected dial failures
history.body:
R-016 / C2-002 (P4.C2 loop 2): track writes and redirect responses across each logical attempt before treating a dial failure as safe to retry. Preserve caller transports, trace callbacks and redirect policy; retain retries for initial dial failures and explicitly idempotent requests.

Regression tests cover 301/302/303/307/308, POST/PATCH, idempotency keys, opt-in retries, custom transports without trace hooks and the default redirect limit. The regression matrix failed before the fix. task test -- httprequest and go test -race -short -count=3 ./httprequest/... pass.

history.subject: feat(httprequest)!: retry only requests that are safe to resend
history.body:
Whether to retry depended only on Metadata.Retriable. A POST that got a
5xx or timed out after the server received it was sent again, up to 5
times by default: duplicate orders, payments or messages, and up to 5
billed completions per llmclient Execute.

A retriable error is now retried only when resending cannot duplicate a
side effect: the method is idempotent (GET or empty, HEAD, OPTIONS, TRACE,
PUT, DELETE), the request carries a non-empty Idempotency-Key or
X-Idempotency-Key header, or the attempt failed while dialling (nothing
was sent). The new RetryConfig.RetryNonIdempotent opts back into retrying
every retriable error. The httprequest and llmclient READMEs document the
rule and the LLM consequence.

Tests: POST/PATCH on 500 sent once; GET, empty method, HEAD, OPTIONS, PUT,
DELETE retried; POST with Idempotency-Key / X-Idempotency-Key retried,
empty key not; RetryNonIdempotent retries POST; POST to a refused
loopback port retried (3 dials).

problem: A Hertz `Run()` bind failure panics the whole process; `Run()` can never return an error
solution: return listen errors from Run and stop handling signals

history.subject: fix(hertz)!: return listen errors from Run and stop handling signals
history.body:
Run called engine.Spin(), which runs the engine in its own goroutine and
always returned nil. When the listen failed (port in use, permission
denied) the netpoll transport panicked in that goroutine and crashed the
process, so callers could not retry, fail readiness or log and exit
cleanly. Spin also installed SIGINT/SIGHUP/SIGTERM handlers that were
never removed and ran their own Shutdown(context.Background()), competing
with the caller's signal.NotifyContext.

Run now calls the engine on the caller's goroutine: it returns nil after
a graceful Shutdown, and a listen failure (returned or raised as the
netpoll panic) becomes an *errorkit.AppError with code
ERR_SYSTEM_CONFIG_INVALID naming the address. No signal handler is
installed. Hertz binds inside its transport, so pre-binding with
server.WithListener would have to happen in the constructor (opening the
port at New); recovering the startup panic on Run's goroutine keeps New
side-effect free. The HTTPServer.Run godoc and both READMEs (quick start
with signal.NotifyContext) document the contract.

Tests: Run on a taken loopback port returns ERR_SYSTEM_CONFIG_INVALID and
the process survives; Run serves /health and returns nil after Shutdown.

problem: Every PostgreSQL failure is `ERR_DB_POSTGRES_ERROR` (retriable, HTTP 503), including not-found, constraint violations and caller cancellation

misconfigured URL, an unsupported scheme or an untrusted TLS certificate

problem: `stringutils.RemoveMarkdownCodeBlock` mangles content that has several fenced blocks and breaks its documented "whole content" rule; `RemoveMarkdownCodeBlock`: narrow fence grammar and its doc comment is attached to the wrong declaration
solution: parse RemoveMarkdownCodeBlock fences line by line

history.subject: fix(stringutils): parse RemoveMarkdownCodeBlock fences line by line
history.body:
The regexp anchored the first opening fence and the last closing fence
of the whole string with a lazy group that spanned intermediate fences,
so two blocks with prose between them were merged into corrupted
content, contradicting the README "whole content" rule. Its info string
was limited to [a-zA-Z]*, so "python3", "c++", "objective-c" or a
trailing space left the fence in place, the one-newline empty block was
not handled, and the doc comment sat on the unexported regexp variable.

RemoveMarkdownCodeBlock now parses lines: one opening fence (>= 3
backticks or tildes, any info string without backticks for backtick
fences), one closing fence of the same character and at least the same
length, and no inner fence line; otherwise the input is returned
unchanged. The doc comment documents the grammar on the function and
the README matches it.

problem: OTLP records get second-precision timestamps and lose large integer precision
solution: write nanosecond RFC 3339 timestamps and keep OTLP integer precision

history.subject: feat(logger)!: write nanosecond RFC 3339 timestamps and keep OTLP integer precision
history.body:
Every log line carried whole Unix epoch seconds in "time", and
OTLPWriter turned that into the record timestamp, so all records within
one second shared a timestamp (ordering and span correlation lost).
OTLPWriter also decoded with json.Unmarshal, so every number became a
float64 and integers above 2^53 (snowflake IDs, nanosecond durations)
were corrupted in the OTLP attributes.

- The per-logger timestamp hook writes the UTC time as RFC 3339 with
  nanoseconds (time.RFC3339Nano), with no allocation and without
  touching zerolog.TimeFieldFormat.
- The Dev console writer formats that field itself (local HH:MM:SS),
  so it no longer depends on the global TimeFieldFormat.
- Init sets zerolog.TimeFieldFormat to time.RFC3339Nano (was
  TimeFormatUnix) so zerolog loggers built outside the SDK match.
- OTLPWriter decodes with UseNumber; integers become Int64 attributes,
  other numbers Float64; the record timestamp is parsed from RFC 3339
  (legacy Unix seconds still accepted). The per-write skip map is
  replaced by a switch.
- README updated.

TestOTLPWriterKeepsTimestampAndIntegerPrecision,
TestOTLPWriterAcceptsLegacyUnixSeconds,
TestLoggerToOTLPKeepsSubSecondTimestamp, TestDevConsoleShowsClockTime.

problem: Registry batch operations commit partially on error; `NewRegistry` skips validation; listings are in random order; `JSONFormatter` fallback builds JSON with `Sprintf` and can emit invalid JSON; Formatter details: `WriteTo`/`Pretty` pick colors from stdout's TTY state, `FormatPlain` omits the payload, the builder pool does nothing; ULID generator: monotonicity not guaranteed under contention, decoder not case-insensitive as documented, dead fallback RNG
solution: all-or-nothing registration, safe JSON fallback, writer colors, monotonic ULIDs; FormatPlain payload emission remains explicitly deferred pending a safe payload policy.

history.subject: fix(errorkit): all-or-nothing registration, safe JSON fallback, writer colors, monotonic ULIDs
history.body:
Registry (C1-016):
- RegisterMany (global and Registry) wrote valid entries until the
  first invalid one and returned an error with the earlier entries
  committed; a conflict inside the batch was not detected. The batch is
  now checked completely first and stored only if every entry passes.
  Merge inherits this and snapshots the source in code order.
- GetAllCodes / GetCodesByGroup / GetCodesByType (global and Registry)
  return sorted codes instead of map order (one shared helper).
- NewRegistry still stores its seed unvalidated (its signature cannot
  return an error); this is now documented.

Formatter (C1-017, C1-018):
- The JSONFormatter fallback interpolated ID and code into a JSON
  template with Sprintf, so a code containing a quote produced invalid
  JSON. It is now marshalled from a struct and carries the marshal
  error as "detail".
- WriteTo chose ANSI colors from stdout's TTY state and wrote escape
  codes into files, sockets and buffers. It now colors only when the
  target writer is itself a terminal (global DisableColors still wins).
- The strings.Builder pool never reused memory (Reset drops the
  buffer) and is removed.
- Printing the payload in FormatPlain is deliberately NOT done (plan:
  could expose payload secrets; revisit after R-001).

ULID (C1-019):
- The clock was read before taking the lock, so a goroutine that waited
  could store an older timestamp after a newer one and break
  monotonicity. The clock is read under the lock and the stored
  timestamp never moves backwards (same millisecond, contention or a
  clock step back all increment the random part); randomness overflow
  moves to the next millisecond instead of sleeping under the lock.
- ParseULID / ValidateULID accept lower case, as the comment promised
  (table-driven decoder).
- The dead time-seeded LCG fallback is removed: crypto/rand.Read does
  not fail since Go 1.24.

README updated (batch semantics, sorted listings, NewRegistry seed,
WriteTo colors, ULID case and monotonicity).

entry, in-batch conflict, identical duplicate),
TestRegistryMergeIsAllOrNothing, TestCodeListingsAreSorted,
TestJSONFormatterFallbackIsValidJSON,
TestWriteToChoosesColorsFromTheTargetWriter, TestULIDNeverGoesBackwards,
TestULIDDecodingIsCaseInsensitive.

history.subject: feat(httprequest)!: cap response body sizes and drain before close
history.body:
Response bodies were read without any limit: io.ReadAll on non-2xx bodies
(only to extract error.code/message), unbounded decoders on 2xx bodies,
and transparent gzip decompression multiplied the cost. An upstream could
exhaust the caller's memory (64 MiB 500 body: 159 MiB allocated per
attempt).

  WithMaxResponseBytes option. A larger body fails with a non-retriable
  httpclient.ERR_EXTERNAL_INVALID_RESPONSE (payload: url,
  max_response_bytes).
- Only the first 64 KiB of a non-2xx body are read.
- Every body is drained (at most 256 KiB) before Close, so the transport
  reuses the connection even when out is nil or decoding stopped early.

Tests: oversized string/bytes/JSON bodies rejected after one attempt,
body at the limit accepted, gzip bomb bounded after decompression, error
body capped at 64 KiB, unread bodies keep one connection, default and
non-positive limit.

problem: `logger.New` mutates process-wide zerolog state (global level and time format)
solution: stop New from mutating zerolog globals

history.subject: fix(logger): stop New from mutating zerolog globals
history.body:
logger.New (through newLoggerWithWriter) called zerolog.SetGlobalLevel
and wrote zerolog.TimeFieldFormat on every construction, so the last
logger built decided the level of every zerolog logger in the process,
and building a logger while another goroutine logged was a data race.

The level is now set on the instance (zerolog.New(w).Level(...)) and the
Unix-seconds timestamp is written by a per-logger hook. Only Init still
applies the process-wide level and time format, as documented
(AGENTS.md §2.3).

and zerolog.TimeFieldFormat are unchanged; new
TestNewLoggersKeepTheirOwnLevel and TestNewWhileLoggingIsRaceFree (-race).

Item: R-050
Findings: C1-001

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

problem: Unsynchronized mutable globals in `errorkit` (`MaxStackDepth`, `ColorsEnabled`, `GenerateID`, exported `ErrorRegistry` map)
solution: unexport mutable globals and back the setters with atomics

history.subject: feat(errorkit)!: unexport mutable globals and back the setters with atomics
history.body:
SetMaxStackDepth, InitFromEnv, DisableColors/EnableColors and
SetIDGenerator wrote plain package variables that NewError, Pretty and
FormatColored read without synchronization (data races), and the
exported ErrorRegistry map could be read or written by consumers without
the registry lock (fatal "concurrent map read and map write").

Per the G1 decision (REMEDIATION_PLAN §12, v2 variant of R-051) the
globals become unexported instead of deprecated:
- MaxStackDepth -> atomic.Int32 behind SetMaxStackDepth / InitFromEnv
- ColorsEnabled -> atomic.Bool behind DisableColors / EnableColors
- GenerateID    -> atomic.Pointer[func() string] behind SetIDGenerator
- ErrorRegistry -> errorRegistry, reachable only through GetMetadata,
  RegisterMany, MustRegister, OverrideMetadata, GetAllCodes,
  GetCodesBy*, NewDefaultRegistry
No other package in the module referenced these variables. README
updated.

Tests: -race tests for every setter running concurrently with NewError /
FormatColored, registry writes concurrent with NewError, and
SetIDGenerator use/reset.

problem: `OverrideMetadata` runs the updater while holding the registry write lock: re-entry deadlocks the whole registry; results are not validated
solution: run OverrideMetadata updater outside the registry lock; make the global OverrideMetadata tests repeatable

Item: R-052 (review fix)
Findings: C1-006

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

history.subject: fix(errorkit): run OverrideMetadata updater outside the registry lock
history.body:
OverrideMetadata (global and Registry) called the caller's updater while
holding the registry write lock: an updater that read the registry
(GetMetadata, NewError, a logger call) deadlocked, and from then on every
NewError in the process blocked. The result was stored without
validation, so an updater could install HTTP status 0 or change Code so
the key and Metadata.Code disagreed.

The updater now runs on a copy without the lock; the result must pass
ValidateMetadata and keep Code (otherwise false is returned and the
entry is unchanged), and it is stored only if the entry did not change
meanwhile (optimistic retry). Documented in the godoc and README.

watchdog, global and Registry), TestOverrideMetadata_RejectsInvalidResult.

nil-Instrumenter fallback) read without synchronization: a data race on

Item: R-053
Findings: C1-013

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

problem: `FileStorage` corrupts data when two instances or processes share a directory (shared fixed temp-file name, in-process lock only); Fixed, predictable temp-file name follows symlinks: an attacker with write access to `baseDir` can overwrite arbitrary files; No durability: writes are never `fsync`ed and a zero-length file is read as an empty list
solution: write FileStorage files through unique synced temp files

history.subject: fix(storage): write FileStorage files through unique synced temp files
history.body:
Every writer used the fixed temp path "<file>.tmp" with os.WriteFile.
Two FileStorage values on one directory truncated and interleaved the
same temp file and renamed it, leaving invalid JSON (all records of the
key lost); a symlink planted at the predictable path was followed; and
nothing was fsynced, while a zero-length file was read as an empty list.

writeUnsafe now creates a unique temp file with os.CreateTemp (O_EXCL,
0600, ".tmp-*", never follows a symlink), writes, syncs, closes, renames
and syncs the directory, removing the temp file on every failure. A
zero-length storage file is reported as corruption. The README and the
type doc state "one FileStorage per directory per host".

Item: R-054
Findings: C4-012, C4-013, C4-016

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

problem: Data written world-readable: directory `0o755`, files `0o644`
solution: create FileStorage directories 0700 and files 0600; reject FileStorage modes that lock the owner out

history.subject: fix(storage): reject FileStorage modes that lock the owner out
history.body:
WithFileMode(0) or WithDirMode(0o600) were accepted and produced a store
its own process could not read, rewrite or traverse; the failure only
showed up on the first operation as ERR_STORAGE_ACCESS_DENIED.

NewFileStorage now validates the options before creating anything: the
directory mode must include owner rwx (0o700) and the file mode owner
read/write (0o600); otherwise it returns a non-retriable
errorkit.ERR_SYSTEM_CONFIG_INVALID. The option docs and the README say
so.

Test: TestFileStorageRejectsModesWithoutOwnerAccess (0, 0400 and 0200
file modes; 0 and 0600 directory modes; no directory is created). All
cases failed before the fix.

Item: R-055 (review fix 5)
Findings: C4-022

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

history.subject: feat(storage)!: create FileStorage directories 0700 and files 0600
history.body:
NewFileStorage created baseDir with 0o755, so any local account could
list the store, and the README did not say who can read stored items.
(Files have been 0o600 since R-054 switched writes to os.CreateTemp;
before that they were 0o644.)

- DefaultDirMode (0o700) and DefaultFileMode (0o600) are the new

- NewFileStorage takes variadic FileStorageOption values: WithDirMode
  (applied when the directory is created, subject to the umask) and

- README section "Permissions".

problem: Hertz `Shutdown(ctx)` is silently capped at 5 s and returns `nil` while requests are still in flight
solution: bound Shutdown by the caller's context and report timeouts

history.subject: fix(hertz): bound Shutdown by the caller's context and report timeouts
history.body:
Hertz capped the caller's context at its ExitWaitTimeout (5 s by
default, not configurable through the adapter) and returned nil even when
requests were still running, so callers closed databases, brokers and
exporters under live handlers. Hertz also waits for idle keep-alive
connections, so any client holding one made Shutdown take the full cap.

- The engine is built with WithExitWaitTime(24h): the context passed to
  Shutdown is the only bound.
- A first middleware counts requests in the handler chain. Shutdown ends
  Hertz's wait as soon as none is in flight, so idle keep-alive
  connections no longer delay it.
- If the context ends while requests are still in flight, Shutdown
  returns ERR_SYSTEM_TIMEOUT_INTERNAL (wrapping ctx.Err()), as
  grpc.Server.Shutdown does.

Tests: ExitWaitTimeout is lifted; a 300 ms in-flight request completes
before Shutdown returns nil; a blocked request with a 200 ms context
yields ERR_SYSTEM_TIMEOUT_INTERNAL; an idle keep-alive connection no
longer delays Shutdown (was 5 s); a 6 s request is drained (skipped with
-short).

Item: R-056
Findings: C2-010

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

problem: `EnableRecovery=false` cannot disable recovery; with `true`, two recovery layers run and Hertz logs panics through its own logger
solution: make EnableRecovery the only, outermost recovery layer

history.subject: fix(hertz)!: make EnableRecovery the only, outermost recovery layer
history.body:
The engine was built with server.Default, which always adds Hertz's own
recovery: EnableRecovery=false could not disable recovery, and with true
two layers ran. Hertz's handler logged the panic value and full stack as
unstructured text through hlog, bypassing the SDK logger, its redaction
and trace correlation, and the SDK RecoveryHandler sat inside the tracing
middleware, so panics there were only seen by Hertz. RecoveryHandler also
dropped its stack argument.

- The engine is built with server.New.
- With EnableRecovery the SDK recovery is installed first (outermost),
  before tracing, the in-flight tracker and audit.
- RecoveryHandler logs one structured line through
  logger.CtxOrGlobal(ctx) with trace_id/span_id and the stack in
  "panic_stack", then aborts with 500.
- With EnableRecovery=false no recovery layer runs and the panic
  propagates, as the option promises.

Tests: EnableRecovery=false lets the handler panic propagate; true gives
500, exactly one structured line with error_code and panic_stack, and no
Hertz "[Recovery]" output.

Item: R-057
Findings: C2-011 (also the hertz RecoveryHandler part of X1-008)

BREAKING CHANGE: with ServerOptions.EnableRecovery=false a handler panic
is no longer recovered by Hertz and crashes the process; keep it true
(the default) or install your own recovery middleware. The recovery log
line gains a panic_stack field and Hertz no longer prints "[Recovery]"
lines.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

problem: No end-to-end bound on the LLM path, and per-attempt budgets multiply on the default path
solution: bound LLM calls end to end by default

history.subject: feat(llmclient)!: bound LLM calls end to end by default
history.body:
Nothing bounded the LLM path: SetupForLLM disables the client timeout and
llmclient.Config.Timeout defaulted to 0 (no deadline), so after headers
arrived a stalled upstream held the goroutine and connection forever. On
the default path the 60 s client timeout applied per attempt, so one Do
without a context deadline could take about 5 minutes, and the 60 s
default dial timeout was far above service-to-service norms.

- llmclient: Config.Timeout 0 now applies the new DefaultTimeout
  (5 min) to the whole Execute; a negative value disables the client-side
  deadline explicitly.
- httprequest: new RetryConfig.MaxElapsed bounds the whole Do (every
  attempt and wait); with the R-072 budget check, a retry that would
  start after it is not made. The README documents that ctx/MaxElapsed
  is the total budget.
- httpclient: new DefaultDialTimeout (10 s) replaces the 60 s dial
  timeout in DefaultConfig.

TestExecuteNoDeadlineWhenTimeoutZero pinned the unbounded default; it is
now TestExecuteNoDeadlineWhenTimeoutNegative (the explicit opt-out keeps
that coverage) and TestExecuteDefaultDeadlineWhenTimeoutZero asserts the
approved default.

Tests: default deadline for Timeout 0, none for Timeout < 0; MaxElapsed
stops a 5-attempt Do with 2 s Retry-After waits within 3 s (synctest);
DefaultDialTimeout <= 10 s and used by DefaultConfig.

Item: R-058
Findings: C2-012

BREAKING CHANGE: llmclient.Config{Timeout: 0} now means a 5-minute
deadline per Execute instead of none (use a negative Timeout for none);
httpclient.DefaultConfig().DialTimeout is 10 s instead of 60 s.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

problem: The server accepts an unbounded number of concurrent streams per connection by default
solution: add ServerConfig.MaxConcurrentStreams

history.subject: feat(grpc): add ServerConfig.MaxConcurrentStreams
history.body:
ServerConfig exposed message sizes and keepalive but not the per-connection
stream limit, and grpc-go's default is math.MaxUint32: one client could
open streams (each with a handler goroutine and flow-control state) until
memory ran out. Only WithRawServerOptions could limit it.

ServerConfig.MaxConcurrentStreams (uint32, 0 = gRPC default) is wired
through grpc.MaxConcurrentStreams. The default is unchanged. README:
Defaults row with a recommended range for servers reachable by untrusted
clients, quick-start value, migration table.

Tests: with MaxConcurrentStreams = 1, a second stream on the same
connection never reaches a handler while the first is open and times out
waiting for stream quota.

Item: R-059
Findings: C3-006 (auto part)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

problem: Recovery is not outermost when an interceptor is passed through `WithRawServerOptions`
solution: document that raw interceptors run outside recovery

history.subject: docs(grpc): document that raw interceptors run outside recovery
history.body:
The server comment claimed recovery runs outermost, which holds only for
interceptors added with WithUnaryInterceptors/WithStreamInterceptors.
grpc-go prepends a grpc.UnaryInterceptor/StreamInterceptor passed through
WithRawServerOptions in front of the whole chain, so a panic there is not
recovered and crashes the process.

- WithRawServerOptions godoc: do not add interceptors there.
- WithUnary/StreamInterceptors godoc: they run inside recovery.
- README: "Interceptors and recovery" section (incl. the open question
  from the audit that handler-spawned goroutines need their own recover)
  and the Defaults row.

Tests: end-to-end over bufconn, a panicking interceptor added with
WithUnaryInterceptors / WithStreamInterceptors is recovered (fixed
codes.Internal status, no panic text) and the server keeps serving; user
interceptors run in order, after recovery and before the handler, for
unary and streaming calls.

Item: R-060
Findings: C3-007

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

problem: There is no client-side deadline facility, and Kitex `RPCTimeout`/`ConnectTimeout` were dropped with no replacement
solution: add WithClientDefaultTimeout

history.subject: feat(grpc): add WithClientDefaultTimeout
history.body:
The client offered no default per-call timeout and the README migration
table dropped Kitex RPCTimeout/ConnectTimeout with no replacement, so a
call made with a context without a deadline could block forever on a hung
upstream.

WithClientDefaultTimeout(d) installs unary and stream client interceptors
(ahead of the user's client interceptors) that apply context.WithTimeout
only when the call context has no deadline; an existing deadline is never
overridden. For streams the timeout context is released when the stream
finishes. d <= 0 keeps today's behavior. README: "Client deadlines"
section, Defaults row, client options and migration table
(RPCTimeout/ConnectTimeout replacements).

Tests: the server sees a deadline of about d for unary and streaming
calls without one; a caller's 1h deadline is not overridden; a hung unary
call and a hung bidi stream end with DeadlineExceeded (with a watchdog so a
regression fails instead of hanging).

Item: R-061
Findings: C3-008

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

problem: Default prefetch is unlimited; the client buffers the whole backlog in memory
solution: default prefetch of 1 instead of unlimited

history.subject: feat(messaging)!: default prefetch of 1 instead of unlimited
history.body:
A queue topology that omits prefetch (or sets 0) used to call Qos(0),
which RabbitMQ treats as unlimited: the broker pushed the whole backlog
into the client's unbounded buffer while handlers ran one message at a
time. Subscribers now use the new DefaultPrefetch (1) in that case;
an explicit prefetch is kept, and a negative one is rejected by
Topology.Validate (R-026). The README documents the default.

Item: R-062
Findings: C5-003

BREAKING CHANGE: queues whose topology omits prefetch now consume with
a prefetch window of 1 instead of unlimited. Set prefetch explicitly to
keep a larger window.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

problem: Ack/Nack errors are discarded; at-least-once redelivery is invisible and undocumented
solution: report failed Ack and Nack instead of discarding them

history.subject: fix(messaging): report failed Ack and Nack instead of discarding them
history.body:
handleDelivery threw away the errors of msg.Ack and msg.Nack. When the
channel dies between a successful handler and its ack, the broker
redelivers the message and the handler runs twice with nothing to
explain it. A failed Ack/Nack is now recorded on the receive span
(ERR_MQ_CHANNEL_ERROR, status Error) and logged at Warn level through
the WithLogger logger (the ctx/global logger otherwise), including the
requeue Nack issued during shutdown. The README documents at-least-once
delivery and that handlers must be idempotent (deduplicate on
event_id).

Item: R-063
Findings: C5-005

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

problem: `Publish` ignores its ctx; the publisher mutex is held across dial and network I/O
solution: honour ctx in Publish and dial outside the mutex; detach the old connection before a reconnect closes it

history.subject: fix(messaging): detach the old connection before a reconnect closes it
history.body:
reconnect closed the previous connection outside the mutex but left
p.conn/p.channel pointing at it until the swap. A Close racing that
reconnect closed the same connection again, got amqp.ErrClosed and
returned a spurious "[ERR_MQ_CONNECTION_FAILED] failed to close
connection". The old link is now detached under the mutex before it is
closed, so Close finds nothing left to close and returns nil while the
reconnect reports ERR_MQ_CLOSED.

Item: R-064 (review follow-up)
Findings: C5-007, C5-008

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

history.subject: fix(messaging): honour ctx in Publish and dial outside the mutex
history.body:
PubSub.Publish now passes its ctx down to the publisher. The new
Publisher.PublishWithContext waits for the publishing turn, reconnects
and publishes under that ctx: an ended ctx never dials, a caller queued
behind a slow reconnect gives up at its own deadline, and the error
wraps ctx.Err() (ERR_MQ_TIMEOUT for a deadline). The dial runs outside
the mutex that guards the connection, so Close is never blocked by an
unreachable broker; reconnects stay single-flight. The ctx also bounds
the TCP connect and the AMQP handshake through amqp.Config.Dial. The
documented "reconnect once more and retry" behaviour is kept.

Item: R-064
Findings: C5-007

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

problem: `Close` is not terminal: `Publish` after `Close` silently re-dials and leaks a connection; `PubSub.Close` does not stop subscribers
solution: make Close terminal and stop subscribers; fail Subscribe with ERR_MQ_CLOSED when Close races it; declare the specific error codes returned by Publish

history.subject: docs(messaging)!: declare the specific error codes returned by Publish
history.body:
R-025 (23afe68) stopped re-wrapping SDK errors, so PubSub.Publish
returns the code of the step that failed instead of always
ERR_MQ_PUBLISH_FAILED. The change was accepted under the approved
R-025b but never declared as breaking. The README Error Codes section
now lists which code each failure produces and tells callers to decide
on Metadata.Retriable or test a specific code with errorkit.HasCode
(added by cluster C1) or errors.As and Code().

Item: R-025, R-025b, R-065 (review follow-up)
Findings: C5-006, C5-008
BREAKING CHANGE: PubSub.Publish now returns the specific ERR_MQ_* code of the failure (ERR_MQ_CONNECTION_FAILED, ERR_MQ_EXCHANGE_ERROR, ERR_MQ_QUEUE_ERROR, ERR_MQ_AUTH_FAILED, ERR_MQ_TIMEOUT, ERR_MQ_CLOSED or ERR_MQ_PUBLISH_FAILED) instead of always ERR_MQ_PUBLISH_FAILED; callers that match ERR_MQ_PUBLISH_FAILED must use errorkit.HasCode or Metadata.Retriable instead. PubSub is no longer comparable with == (it holds a context.CancelFunc since f111a23), as gorelease reports.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

history.subject: fix(messaging): fail Subscribe with ERR_MQ_CLOSED when Close races it
history.body:
Subscribe checked the PubSub lifetime before registering the AfterFunc
that cancels it on Close. A Close landing between the two let Subscribe
dial a subscriber connection once and return nil. Subscribe now
registers first and checks afterwards, so a Close before the check
returns ERR_MQ_CLOSED without dialing and a Close after it cancels the
subscription. An unexported test hook marks the former race window.

Item: R-065 (review follow-up)
Findings: C5-008

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

history.subject: feat(messaging)!: make Close terminal and stop subscribers
history.body:
Publisher.Close now records a closed state: later publishes fail with
the new non-retriable ERR_MQ_CLOSED and never re-dial, a reconnect that
completes after Close closes its connection instead of reviving the
publisher, and a second Close returns nil. PubSub.Close also cancels
every Subscribe call it started (the in-flight message is requeued and
Subscribe returns nil); Subscribe after Close fails with ERR_MQ_CLOSED.
PubSub.Publish no longer walks the retry policy for a non-retriable
error. Subscribers now dial through the same seam as the publisher.

Item: R-065
Findings: C5-008

BREAKING CHANGE: PubSub.Close stops active Subscribe calls (they used
to keep consuming until their own ctx ended), and Publish or Subscribe
after Close return ERR_MQ_CLOSED instead of silently opening a new
connection.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

problem: Retry of a multi-routing-key publish re-sends keys that already succeeded; nested retries multiply attempts
solution: retry publishes per routing key with one retry layer

history.subject: feat(messaging)!: retry publishes per routing key with one retry layer
history.body:
PubSub.Publish now retries each routing key of the binding on its own,
so a retry after a partial failure no longer re-sends keys the broker
already confirmed (duplicate deliveries with the same event_id). When
the queue has a retry policy it is the only retry layer and maxAttempts
is the number of publish attempts per routing key; the publisher's own
reconnect + single retry now applies only to queues without a policy
and to the standalone Publisher. A channel whose publish failed is not
reused by the next attempt.

Item: R-066
Findings: C5-009

BREAKING CHANGE: for queues with a retry policy, publish attempt and
dial counts change: maxAttempts attempts per routing key instead of up
to 2 x maxAttempts attempts for the whole event, and completed routing
keys are not re-sent on retry.

problem: `NewPostgresClient` cannot be cancelled: no `context.Context`, fixed 5 s `context.Background()` budget; Constructors that do network I/O handle `context` inconsistently
solution: add cancellable database and messaging setup; preserve streaming body and subscription lifetime regressions

history.subject: test: preserve streaming body and subscription lifetime regressions
history.body: P4.XP review loop 1 N2; R-049 and R-067. Promote independently mutation-verified one-byte JSON suffix and Subscribe lifetime probes into permanent tests, preserving all existing assertions.

history.subject: feat(connections): add cancellable database and messaging setup
history.body: R-067; C4-004; X1-009. Add context constructors, configurable PostgreSQL connection timeout, and cancellation of AMQP handshakes and channel setup. Construction contexts do not own successfully created instances; callers retain Close ownership. Local stalled peers and fake channel setup cover cancellation without external services.

problem: Defaults silently override URI options and make `MaxPoolSize < 10` fail at start-up
solution: let URI options win over SDK defaults

history.subject: feat(mongo)!: let URI options win over SDK defaults
history.body:
NewWithInstrumenter applied the URI and then called every Set* with
values from applyDefaults, so maxPoolSize, minPoolSize, retryWrites,
connectTimeoutMS, serverSelectionTimeoutMS and maxIdleTimeMS in the
connection string were discarded. The default MinPoolSize of 10 also
made any MaxPoolSize below 10 fail validation at start-up.

clientOptions now resolves each option as: non-zero Config field, else
the URI value, else the SDK default; the default MinPoolSize is clamped
to the effective MaxPoolSize. applyDefaults is gone; its three
RetryWrites tests now exercise clientOptions with the same assertions
and a URI that sets the opposite value. The README documents the
precedence.

Item: R-068
Findings: C4-011

BREAKING CHANGE: options set in the MongoDB URI are no longer replaced by
SDK defaults, and the default MinPoolSize is clamped to MaxPoolSize, so
the effective pool and retry settings change for URIs that carry

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

problem: Cursor-returning `Find` spans close before iteration; `Ping`/`Close` untraced; start-up ping ignores `ServerSelectionTimeout`
solution: trace cursor iteration and size the start-up ping budget

history.subject: fix(mongo): trace cursor iteration and size the start-up ping budget
history.body:
- tracingCollection.Find ended its span when Find returned, so
  Cursor.All (getMore round trips and decoding) ran outside any span.
  Find now returns a tracingCursor whose All opens
  "mongo.<collection>.find.all".
- tracingClientPort.Ping and Close were untraced; they open "mongo.ping"
  and "mongo.close".
- The start-up ping used a fixed 5 s, so a ServerSelectionTimeout of
  30 s for a slow cluster still failed at 5 s. The budget is now
  max(5s, effective ServerSelectionTimeout) via startupPingTimeout.
- The clean-up Disconnect after a failed ping used an unbounded
  context.Background(); it now uses
  context.WithTimeout(context.WithoutCancel(ctx), 5s).

Item: R-069
Findings: C4-019

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

problem: Connection options are hard-wired: no TLS config for `amqps://`, no dial timeout or properties; heartbeat detection is slower than documented
solution: add TLS, heartbeat, dial timeout and connection name options

history.subject: feat(messaging): add TLS, heartbeat, dial timeout and connection name options

solution: jitter retry backoff and honor Retry-After

history.subject: feat(httprequest)!: jitter retry backoff and honor Retry-After
history.body:
Retry delays were deterministic (100, 200, 400, 800 ms) and Retry-After
was never read, so every client instance retried a rate-limited upstream
in lockstep and before the advertised window.

- The wait before a retry is a random duration in [0, backoff] (full
  jitter); the backoff ceiling still doubles from InitialDelay up to
  MaxDelay.
- A Retry-After header (delay-seconds or HTTP-date) on a failed response
  sets the wait exactly; a value above MaxDelay ends the retries and
  returns the error.
- When the wait would outlast the context deadline, Do returns the last
  upstream error at once instead of sleeping into ERR_NETWORK_TIMEOUT.

Tests (testing/synctest, scripted RoundTripper, no network): jittered
gaps stay under each backoff cap and fall below it; Retry-After in
seconds and as an HTTP date; Retry-After above MaxDelay and beyond the
ctx deadline stop retrying with no wait; parseRetryAfter table.

history.subject: fix(logger): send every line with a backslash through full redaction
history.body:
The R-130 byte pre-filter normalized the raw line (letters and digits
only) and skipped redaction when no sensitive needle appeared. zerolog
writes control characters in keys as two-character JSON escapes (\b \f
\n \r \t): the scan kept the escape letter while the decoded key drops
the control character, so keys such as "to\tken", "api\rkey" and
"pass\nword" were written in clear to stdout and OTLP. A "\/" inside a
nested JSON string also hid "://", leaking URL passwords
(payload {"url":"postgres:\/\/u:s3cr3tpw@h/db"}).

Any line that contains a backslash now takes the full decode/redact
path (this subsumes the previous \u check). Lines without escapes keep
the zero-allocation fast path (BenchmarkLoggerInfoPlain: 0 allocs/op).
README cost paragraph updated.

Tests: TestRedactingWriterSlowPathTriggers gains the \t, \r, \n, \b/\f
key cases and the escaped-slash URL cases (nested and plain);
TestLoggerRedactsKeysWithEscapedControlCharacters checks the same keys
end to end through newLoggerWithWriter(&buf, Prod). All fail on the
previous code.

Item: R-134 (review fix 2)
Findings: C4-017, C4-018

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

history.subject: fix(storage): never read or append through a symlink at a key's path
history.body:
R-134 (d27a2ff) appended in place with os.OpenFile(<hex>.jsonl,
O_WRONLY|O_APPEND), which follows a symlink planted at the final path:
Append("k", x) appended to the link's target, and List/GetAll read the
target's content as the key's data (the same held for the legacy .json
path).

Storage files are now opened through openRegular: Lstat must report a
regular file, the open adds O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK on Unix
(storage/open_unix.go; no-op elsewhere), and os.SameFile(Lstat, f.Stat)
must hold, which closes the window between the check and the open.
A symlink or other non-regular file at a key's path is not data: List
reports the key absent, GetAll skips it, and Append replaces the link
with a regular file through the atomic temp-file rename. If the path
stops being a regular file between the read and the in-place append,
appendLine writes nothing and Append falls back to the atomic rewrite.
The README now states the no-follow guarantee for the final path.

Tests: a symlink at <hex>.jsonl is neither read nor written and is
replaced by a regular file; a symlink at the legacy .json path is not
read; appendLine refuses a symlink without writing. The first two
failed on d27a2ff (List returned the target's items).

history.subject: feat(storage)!: store FileStorage logs as JSON Lines appended in place
history.body:
Every FileStorage.Append read the key's JSON array, appended,
re-encoded the whole list with MarshalIndent and rewrote the file, so
building a log was quadratic in both CPU and bytes written; List also
ran a redundant Stat before reading.

- Current files are <hex key>.jsonl: one compact JSON value per line.
  Append adds one line with O_APPEND and fsyncs it; a new key, a legacy
  file and a file with a torn last line are written atomically through
  the existing temp-file + rename path, so a file always starts with a
  complete line.
- Reader for the old format: <hex key>.json (one JSON array) is still
  read by List and GetAll and is converted to .jsonl by the next Append;
  if both files exist the .jsonl wins; Delete and Clear remove both.
- Corruption rules: an empty file, a file without a complete line, or a
  complete line that does not decode is ERR_STORAGE_CORRUPTED; bytes
  after the last newline (an append torn by a crash, never
  acknowledged) are ignored and dropped by the next Append.
- MaxFileKeyLength is 124 (the ".jsonl" suffix is one byte longer).
- Ownership (GetAll/Clear) now requires the exact lowercase hex name
  that fileNameForKey or legacyFileNameForKey produces.
- The redundant Stat in List is gone; the receiver is renamed from fs
  to s so it no longer shadows io/fs.

BenchmarkFileStorageAppend (build a log of n records on one key,
-benchtime=3x -count=6, tmpfs, i7-1260P; medians computed by hand
because benchstat could not be installed in this environment):

  records=100   6.46ms -> 2.45ms   1.89MB -> 0.97MB/op
  records=1000  350.6ms -> 187.9ms 178.8MB -> 84.6MB/op

Append still reads and decodes the whole file because the
AppendLogStorager contract returns the full list, so reads stay O(n)
per call; only the write side is now O(1). allocs/op rose
(36,810 -> 515,754 at 1000) because each line is decoded separately;
a json.Decoder stream was slower.

Test changes: TestFileStorageAppendLeavesNoTempFiles now checks that
every line is valid JSON (the whole file is no longer one JSON value),
and the ACCESS_DENIED case in TestStorageErrorCodes also makes the
key's file read-only, because an append now writes the file in place
instead of creating a file in the directory. New tests cover in-place
appends (same inode), the legacy reader and conversion, legacy
corruption, precedence of .jsonl over .json, Clear of legacy files,
torn last lines and corrupt lines.

history.subject: build(scripts): treat unparsable go vet output as a tool failure
history.body:
The go vet parser in scripts/staticanalysis.sh turned every line with
two colons into a JSON finding with printf. A panicking go vet (stack
lines such as "\t/…/main.go:12 +0x1d") produced a non-numeric "line",
and messages with backslashes or tabs produced invalid JSON; in both
cases `jq -s` failed and, under `set -e`, the runner exited 5 instead
of reporting TOOL FAILURE (exit 2) or the findings.

- awk only accepts "file:line[:col]: msg" with a numeric line and emits
  TSV; any other non-blank, non-"#" line goes to an "unparsable" list.
- jq builds the JSON from the TSV, so quotes, backslashes and tabs are
  escaped correctly.
- A failing go vet (non-zero exit) with no parsed diagnostic, or with
  any unparsable line, is a tool failure (exit 2).

Validated with a fake `go` shim (scratchpad, not committed; QG_SKIP_SC
and QG_SKIP_SEMGREP set), new vs. previous runner:
  vet panic, exit 2                     -> 2 (was 5)
  one diagnostic + panic, exit 1        -> 2 (was 1, panic hidden)
  diagnostics with quotes/backslash/tab -> 1, valid JSON (was 5)
  clean, exit 0                         -> 0 (was 0)
